subject: RE: Data deletion / RTBF follow-up and timelines
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: RTBF / deletion requirements (post-call)

Hi Jordan / Samira —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the open items we promised to follow up on: 

- Scope: You indicated the scope is customer PII (names, emails), account-level embeddings and any generated artifacts tied to customer IDs. Need confirmation whether logs that contain PII (request/response bodies) should be deleted or can be redacted/anonymized.
- Desired SLA: You mentioned a target of 30 days for full deletion of live store data and 90 days for backups, but requested we explore shorter windows for backups where possible.
- Residency: EU-only tenancy for EU accounts (data-at-rest and initial deletion workflow).
- Audit: You asked for a deletion confirmation certificate and a description of what we purge vs. what is retained for audit/security.

Attached is a short outline of our RTBF process (redwood-rtbf-process.pdf). High-level next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to confirm tech constraints for backup snapshots and KMS key lifecycle.
2) Priya to review DPA/DPA appendix language for deletion certificate/attestation.
3) Camila to propose a mutual action plan and target dates (we'll include any exceptions).

Can you confirm the scope points above (especially whether logs must be fully deleted vs. redacted) and whether 30d live / 90d backups is acceptable as an initial SLA?

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-rtbf-process.pdf (1 page summary)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fintechco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Nadeem <samira@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RTBF / deletion requirements (post-call)

Camila —

Thanks for the recap and the attachment — very helpful. Confirming the following from our side: 

- Scope: Yes — all customer-identifiable data (PII) stored in model inputs/outputs, embeddings that can be linked back to customer IDs, and any derived artifacts that contain PII must be removed on request.
- Logs: We need request/response logs with PII removed entirely. We can accept redaction/anonymization only if it is provably irreversible; otherwise full deletion.
- SLA: 30 days for live data is our target. Backups: ideally 30 days but we understand legacy snapshot retention policies may require up to 90 days — we need an estimate of the earliest possible purge for backups and any compensating controls.
- Residency: EU data must remain in EU regions and deletion must be performed in EU systems.
- Audit/certificate: We require a signed deletion attestation that lists what was deleted, timestamps, and the retention windows for any items not immediately deletable (e.g., immutable cold snapshots).

Can you provide a proposed workflow that shows what happens when we submit a subject access request / deletion (who owns each step, expected durations, and what evidence we'll receive)? Also please call out KMS/HSM behavior — how do you handle key destruction and whether that achieves crypto-delete for backups?

Jordan
Director, Security & Privacy
FintechCo
jordan.lee@fintechco.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: RTBF / deletion requirements (post-call)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clarity. We're aligned on the ask; below is a practical workflow and the current constraints to surface so you have a realistic expectation: 

Proposed RTBF workflow (draft):
1) FintechCo submits RTBF request via support + signed DPA appendix or portal (day 0).
2) Redwood validates request and scopes related artifacts (0-3 days).
3) Live store deletion (primary DB / object store): targeted deletion for objects, embedding indices, and derived artifacts (3-30 days depending on dataset size and cross-account indexing).
4) Log redaction/deletion: if logs contain unredacted PII we will remove those entries; complete redaction may require log reprocessing (3-30 days).
5) Backup snapshots: warm snapshots (nearline/short-term) — eligible for targeted purge as soon as snapshot retention policies allow; cold/immutable snapshots may be retained up to 90 days on current infra. We will provide a timeline per snapshot and pursue expedited purge for dedicated accounts where we control the full snapshot lifecycle.
6) KMS/HSM: we can schedule key rotation and key-destruction workflows for customer-specific keys. Crypto-delete via KMS key destruction is possible for backups encrypted with customer-managed keys; for provider-managed keys we will provide attestation and timelines.
7) Certificate: we will produce a deletion attestation listing items deleted, timestamps, and items pending with expected purge dates (PDF).

Constraints/notes: 
- For Hosted accounts, certain immutable snapshots (cloud provider snapshots) may have minimum retention windows. We can negotiate earlier purge for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Evidence: we can provide deletion logs and attestation; we do not currently produce per-request DB audit snapshots for every delete (we can include this in SOC2 evidence scope with Legal).

Next steps: Marcus and Priya are cc'd to confirm the backup/KMS specifics and draft the deletion attestation language. I've attached a first-pass mutual action plan (rtbf-maction-plan-draft.docx) with timelines to start. Please confirm whether a 30d live / up-to-90d backup SLA is acceptable as an initial commitment while we work on reducing the backup window for you.

Thanks —
Camila

Attachment: rtbf-maction-plan-draft.docx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: internal: Backup / snapshot constraints for RTBF

Camila / Priya —

Quick internal notes on infra constraints so we can set expectations for Jordan: 
- Hosted (multi-tenant) backups: snapshots are managed by cloud provider with immutable retention policies. We can issue targeted deletion for objects and indices, but snapshot-level purge often requires provider support and can take up to 90 days depending on the provider's retention SLA.
- Dedicated: if FintechCo moves to Dedicated we can control snapshot lifecycle and support a 30d backup purge SLA via configuration/retention policy change and coordinate provider snapshot deletes.
- KMS: For customer-managed keys (CMK) in Dedicated/Private, crypto-delete works by key destruction; for provider-managed keys in Hosted, we can schedule key rotation and provide attestation but cannot instantly crypto-delete provider-managed backups.
- Logs: we can reprocess logs to remove PII; that is operational work but standard.

I recommend we propose two tiers in the MAP: Tier 1 (Hosted): 30d live, up to 90d backups with attestation; Tier 2 (Dedicated): 30d live, 30d backups + crypto-delete with CMK. Priya — please add the legal language around attestation and exception handling.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Samira Nadeem <samira@fintechco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: RTBF / deletion requirements (post-call)

Jordan / Samira —

Thanks for the confirmation and for the patience while we validated constraints. Summary and proposed next steps: 

- Summary: We can commit to 30 days for live-store deletion. For backups, Hosted accounts may have up to 90-day snapshot retention due to provider constraints; Dedicated/Private can be configured to 30 days and support crypto-delete via customer-managed keys. Logs containing PII will be removed or irreversibly redacted per your preference — we suggest redaction only if you require an anonymization proof, otherwise we will delete.

- Deliverables we will send by EOD Mon: 
  * Finalized mutual action plan with two tiers (Hosted / Dedicated) and timelines (rtbf-maction-plan-final.docx).
  * Deletion attestation template for review (PDF).
  * DPA appendix language for signature and a DocuSign link for the DPA (https://docusign.com/abc123).

Next steps for FintechCo: please confirm which tier you prefer (Hosted with attestation or Dedicated with CMK and 30d backups) and whether you require full log deletions (vs. irreversible redaction). Once we have that, we'll schedule a brief walk-through (30 minutes) with Marcus on the technical steps and Priya on attestation language.

Looking forward —

Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
